key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Gradual over weeks to months. LOCATION: Bilateral, often upper lobes. DURATION: Chronic, months. CHARACTER: Chronic cough, chest pain. AGGRAVATING: Lying flat, exertion. RELIEVING: Antitubercular drugs. TIMING: Chronic, persistent. SEVERITY: Moderate to severe (5-8/10). ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: Chronic cough, hemoptysis, fever, night sweats, weight loss, fatigue. KEY POSITIVES: Chronic cough, hemoptysis, fever, weight loss. KEY NEGATIVES: No wheezing (unless reactive airway disease).
